Slice: Return Tool

Intent

Let a borrower bring a tool back and end their loan themselves, from My Loans. The tool is then back in the shed, for the next holder or for anyone to borrow. The return records whether it was late, which is what counts toward a neighbor being flagged.

Trigger & Actor

The borrower, from their own My Loans screen, for one of their own loans. My Loans offers Return on every loan it lists (INV-MYL-12), including overdue loans, loans whose tool was retired while out, and loans of a suspended neighbor. The shed manager does not record returns; a tool that never comes back is recorded lost instead (Record Tool Lost).

Command / Input

Command: Return Tool

A NeighborId or LoanId is a UUID.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes The neighbor returning, who must be the one making the request and the loan's borrower (INV-RET-1).
loanId LoanId yes The loan to end. Must be a loan that has been checked out (INV-RET-11), and still out (INV-RET-2).

There is no field for the tool's condition: nothing about it is recorded on return. A damaged tool is the shed manager's to retire.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen My Loans @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Tool Returned → context Loans Read by: My Loans (the loan drops off), Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (the tool is back in the shed), Holds To Fulfill (a returned tool with holds waiting), Overdue Loans To Notify and Undelivered Notices (the loan has ended), and Neighbors To Flag and Flagged Neighbors (whether the return was late).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
loanId LoanId yes From the command.
toolId ToolId yes The loan's tool, from its Tool Checked Out. Carried so views about tools and holds match on the tool directly.
toolName Text yes Set by the system: the tool's name on the loan's Tool Checked Out.
dueDate Date yes Set by the system: the loan's due date in force at the moment of return (Tool Checked Out.dueDate, moved by any Loan Extended), the date late was judged against.
returnedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.
returnedOn Date yes Set by the system: the calendar date of returnedAt in the shed's local time zone.
late Bool yes Set by the system: yes when returnedOn is after the loan's due date in force at the moment of return (INV-RET-4).

The event never changes. returnedOn and late are worked out once, by the command's handler, so every view reads the same answer.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Tool Returned ends the loan in My Loans, Overdue Loans To Notify and Undelivered Notices; puts the tool back in the shed on Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (or drops a tool retired while out); adds a tool with holds waiting to Holds To Fulfill; and gives Neighbors To Flag and Flagged Neighbors a late or on-time return. Each is specified in its own doc, and all are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

Once a loan is returned, no overdue notice goes out for it (INV-OLN-4, Overdue Loans To Notify). A returned tool with no holds waiting is available to borrow straight away; one with holds waiting is reserved, and until Hold Fulfilled is recorded only the neighbor at the front of the queue may check it out (INV-CHK-3a, Check Out Tool). Late returns count toward a neighbor being flagged, 3 within 90 days (Neighbors To Flag). Those rules are owned by those slices.

  • INV-RET-1: The borrower returns their own loan themselves, from My Loans.
    • The request must come from the neighbor it names, and the loan must be theirs. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch. The shed manager does not record returns.
  • INV-RET-2: Only a loan that is still out can be returned, and only once.
    • A loan ended by the shed manager recording the tool lost can't be returned.
    • A closed account never has a loan out, because an account can't be closed while tools are on loan (INV-CLS-7, Close Account).
  • INV-RET-3: Returning a tool records only Tool Returned.
    • Setting the tool aside for the first waiting hold is a separate system reaction to the return, recorded as Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold).
  • INV-RET-4: A return is late when it happens after the loan's due date: from the start of the day after the due date, in the shed's local time.
    • A return on the due date itself is on time. The due date is the one in force at the moment of return: the latest Loan Extended's dueDate, or Tool Checked Out's if never extended.
    • Tool Returned records the answer as late, with the date of return as returnedOn.
  • INV-RET-5: An overdue loan can be returned.
  • INV-RET-7: A suspended neighbor can return a tool.
  • INV-RET-9: A tool retired while on loan can still be returned.
    • The return ends the loan as usual. The tool stays retired: it doesn't come back into the Tool Catalog or Tool Inventory, and no hold is waiting on it, because retiring it ended its holds.
  • INV-RET-10: Returning a loan that this borrower has already returned succeeds and records nothing.
    • So a double submit, or a retry after a lost response, never records a second return.
  • INV-RET-11: The loan must have been checked out.
  • INV-RET-12: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path: on-time return, no holds (INV-RET-1, INV-RET-3, INV-RET-4)
    • Given: Ana (N1) has the cordless drill (T1) on loan L1, due 12 October, and no holds are waiting on it
    • When: at 15:00 on 11 October, shed time, Ana returns L1 from My Loans
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded for L1, with toolId T1, the time it was recorded, returnedOn 11 October, and late no. Nothing else is recorded.
  • Return on the due date (INV-RET-4)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October
    • When: Ana returns L1 at 23:59 on 12 October, shed time
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded with returnedOn 12 October, late no.
  • Late return (INV-RET-4, INV-RET-5)
    • Given: L1 was due 12 October, and Overdue Notice Sent has been recorded for it
    • When: Ana returns L1 at 00:05 on 13 October, shed time
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded with returnedOn 13 October, late yes.
  • Return after an extension (INV-RET-4)
    • Given: L1 was due 12 October, and Loan Extended moved its due date to 19 October
    • When: Ana returns L1 on 15 October
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded with late no, judged against 19 October.
  • Return with a hold waiting (INV-RET-3)
    • Given: Ana has L1, and Ben's hold on T1 is at the front of the queue
    • When: Ana returns L1
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded. No Hold Fulfilled is recorded by this command; setting T1 aside for Ben is Fulfill Hold's.
  • Suspended neighbor returns a tool (INV-RET-7)
    • Given: Ana is suspended and has L1 out
    • When: Ana returns L1 from My Loans
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded for L1.
  • Returning a tool that was retired while on loan (INV-RET-9)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder (T2) on loan L2, and Tool Retired was recorded for T2 while it was out
    • When: Ana returns L2 from My Loans
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded for L2, with toolId T2. T2 stays retired.
  • The same return twice (INV-RET-10)
    • Given: Tool Returned was recorded for L1
    • When: Ana's same Return Tool request for L1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Loan already recorded lost (INV-RET-2)
    • Given: Tool Lost was recorded for Ana's loan L3
    • When: Ana asks to return L3
    • Then: refused with loan-ended: "This loan has ended." No event is recorded.
  • Someone else's loan (INV-RET-1)
    • Given: Ana has L1 out
    • When: Ben asks, for himself, to return L1
    • Then: refused with not-your-loan: "You can only return your own loans." No event is recorded.
  • A request in someone else's name (INV-RET-1)
    • Given: Ana has L1 out
    • When: a request from Ben asks to return L1 for Ana
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only return loans for yourself." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown loan (INV-RET-11)
    • Given: no loan has ID L9
    • When: Ana asks to return L9
    • Then: refused with loan-not-found: "There is no such loan." No event is recorded.
  • Not signed in (INV-RET-12)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: a request for returning a tool arrives
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the borrower on the My Loans screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-RET-12): a request with no sign-in is refused first.
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-RET-1).
  3. loan-not-found (INV-RET-11).
  4. not-your-loan (INV-RET-1).
  5. If Tool Returned is already recorded for the loan, the request is a repeat: it succeeds and records nothing (INV-RET-10).
  6. loan-ended, if Tool Lost is recorded for the loan (INV-RET-2).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-RET-12
requester-mismatch You can only return loans for yourself. INV-RET-1
loan-not-found There is no such loan. INV-RET-11
not-your-loan You can only return your own loans. INV-RET-1
loan-ended This loan has ended. INV-RET-2

requester-mismatch and loan-not-found can only come from a faulty or impersonating caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name. The names mean the same conditions as in Extend Loan, and loan-ended uses the same sentence.

Suspension, an overdue loan and a retired tool never stop a return; there is no refusal for them.

Idempotency: a return is identified by its loan. A repeat after the loan was returned succeeds and records nothing. A loan ended by Tool Lost is refused, because returning it would be a different outcome from the one recorded.

Requests at the same moment: each Return Tool is decided against the loan's events as already recorded, one at a time per loan. Of a return and a Record Tool Lost for the same loan at once, whichever is decided first is recorded; the other finds the loan ended (a return then gets loan-ended, or succeeds as a repeat if the first was itself a return).

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a borrower may return only their own loans (INV-RET-1); the shed manager doesn't record returns. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch.
  • PII & compliance: Tool Returned holds no name or email; it records which loan ended, when, and whether it was late.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time rule above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (this slice): loanId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • These match slices/check-out-tool.md and slices/extend-loan.md. Record Tool Lost is specified in a slice not yet written in depth; it is checked against this key when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Loans, Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog, Holds To Fulfill, Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Neighbors To Flag and Flagged Neighbors. Fulfill Hold reacts to a returned tool with holds waiting.

Open Questions

None.

  • Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors were folded into the Neighbors view (model reshape 2026-11-01, merged-from on slices/neighbors.md v2): reword this doc's mentions of them to Neighbors

Slice: Overdue Loans To Notify

Intent

The list of overdue loans whose borrowers have not yet been sent an overdue notice. The overdue notice gateway works through it, so each borrower with an overdue loan is emailed once, as soon as the loan is overdue. Each item carries everything the email needs, so the gateway looks nothing up elsewhere.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the Overdue Notice Gateway, a system reaction in the Send Overdue Notice slice. No person reads this list, and it has no screen.
  • What the gateway does with it: for each loan on the list, it hands one notice to the email provider and records Overdue Notice Sent (Send Overdue Notice slice). How often it checks the list is that slice's concern.

Read Model / View

  • View: Overdue Loans To Notify built from events: "Neighbor Registered", "Tool Checked Out", "Loan Extended", "Overdue Notice Sent", "Neighbor Email Changed", "Tool Returned", "Tool Lost"
  • Consumed by: the Overdue Notice Gateway (Send Overdue Notice). Internal: no ui.
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events: a change shows shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Whether a loan is overdue is worked out when the list is read, from dueDate and today's date in the shed's local time zone, so a loan is on the list from the first read after midnight following its due date.

The view keeps one row for every open loan that hasn't been sent a notice; the query returns only the overdue ones. LoanId, ToolId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

Field Type Source / Notes
loanId LoanId Tool Checked Out.loanId.
toolId ToolId Tool Checked Out.toolId.
neighborId NeighborId Tool Checked Out.neighborId: the borrower.
dueDate Date Tool Checked Out.dueDate, replaced by each Loan Extended.dueDate for this loan.
toolName Text Tool Checked Out.toolName.
borrowerName Text Derived: Neighbor Registered.name for neighborId, copied under this name.
borrowerEmail Text Derived: Neighbor Registered.email for neighborId, replaced by each Neighbor Email Changed.email for that neighbor, copied under this name. Always the current one.
overdue Bool Derived: yes when today's date in the shed's local time zone is after dueDate (INV-OLN-1). Worked out when the list is read.

Bookkeeping. To fill toolName, borrowerName and borrowerEmail the moment a loan starts, the view keeps the name and current email of every registered neighbor, and the name of every tool, not only those on a row. This is never returned except on the rows the query returns.

When a row leaves the view. A loan's row is removed when Overdue Notice Sent, Tool Returned or Tool Lost is recorded for it (INV-OLN-8). Nothing puts it back.

Queries

  • List loans to notify. Takes nothing. Returns every row whose overdue is yes, with loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate, toolName, borrowerName and borrowerEmail. There is no paging. The order doesn't matter to the gateway, which sends one notice per loan.

Invariants / Business Rules

A loan is ready for its notice as soon as it joins the list. When the email goes out, with no quiet hours, is Send Overdue Notice's rule (INV-OVN-6, Send Overdue Notice).

  • INV-OLN-1: A loan is on the list from the start of the day after its due date, in the shed's local time, while the tool is still out and no overdue notice has been sent for it.
    • Overdue is worked out by comparing the due date with today. No event marks a loan overdue; the loan joins the list because the date has passed.
  • INV-OLN-2: A loan's due date is the one set at checkout, moved by each extension.
    • A loan extended before it became overdue joins the list only once its new due date has passed.
  • INV-OLN-3: Once an overdue notice is sent for a loan, the loan leaves the list and never comes back.
    • One notice per loan. An overdue loan can't be extended (INV-EXT-5, Extend Loan), so it stays overdue until it ends, and no second notice goes out.
  • INV-OLN-4: When the tool is returned, or the shed manager records it lost, its loan leaves the list.
    • A loan that ends this way before its notice went out never gets a notice.
    • A closed account never has a loan on the list, because an account can't be closed while tools are on loan (INV-CLS-7, Close Account).
    • A loan whose tool is retired while it is out stays on the list and still gets its notice: the loan carries on until the tool is returned or recorded lost.
  • INV-OLN-6: Each loan on the list carries everything the notice needs: the borrower's name and email, the tool's name, and the due date.
    • The borrower's name comes from Neighbor Registered, and the email is the borrower's current one: Neighbor Registered sets it, Neighbor Email Changed replaces it. The tool's name and the due date come from Tool Checked Out, the due date moved by any Loan Extended. The gateway looks nothing up elsewhere.
  • INV-OLN-8: A loan leaves the list only when an overdue notice is sent for it, when the tool is returned, or when the tool is recorded lost.
    • A notice that later fails to deliver doesn't put the loan back on the list. The failure is shown to the shed manager on Undelivered Notices, and no further attempt is made.
  • INV-OLN-9: Applying the same event twice leaves the list as if it had been applied once.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Loan not yet overdue (INV-OLN-1)
    • Given: Tool Checked Out was recorded for loan L1: Ana (N1) borrowing the cordless drill (T1), due 12 October
    • When: the list is read at 23:59 on 12 October, shed time
    • Then: L1 is not returned.
  • Loan becomes overdue (INV-OLN-1, INV-OLN-6)
    • Given: Neighbor Registered was recorded for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, and L1, Ana's loan of T1 "Cordless drill", is due 12 October, still out
    • When: the list is read at 00:00 on 13 October, shed time
    • Then: L1 is returned, with toolName "Cordless drill", borrowerName "Ana Ruiz", borrowerEmail ana@example.org, and dueDate 12 October.
  • Extended before it became overdue (INV-OLN-2)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October
    • When: Loan Extended is recorded for L1 on 10 October, with the due date 19 October
    • Then: L1 is not returned when the list is read on 13 October, and is returned from 00:00 on 20 October if still out.
  • Overdue notice sent (INV-OLN-3, INV-OLN-8)
    • Given: L1 is on the list
    • When: Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for L1
    • Then: L1 leaves the list, and is never returned again while the drill is out.
  • Returned before the notice (INV-OLN-4)
    • Given: L1 is on the list
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for L1 before any notice is sent
    • Then: L1 leaves the list, and no notice is sent for it.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-OLN-4)
    • Given: L1 is on the list
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for L1
    • Then: L1 leaves the list, and no notice is sent for it.
  • Tool retired while out (INV-OLN-4)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October and still out, and Tool Retired was recorded for T1 on 11 October
    • When: the list is read at 00:00 on 13 October
    • Then: L1 is returned, ready for its notice.
  • Borrower changes their email (INV-OLN-6)
    • Given: L1 is on the list, carrying ana@oldmail.example
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, to ana@example.org
    • Then: L1 stays on the list, now carrying ana@example.org, so the notice goes to the new address.
  • Email changed before the loan is overdue (INV-OLN-6)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October, and N1's email was changed to ana@example.org on 10 October
    • When: the list is read at 00:00 on 13 October
    • Then: L1 is returned carrying ana@example.org.
  • Several borrowers (INV-OLN-1)
    • Given: L1 (Ana, due 12 October) and L2 (Ben, due 14 October) are both out
    • When: the list is read on 13 October
    • Then: only L1 is returned.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-OLN-9)
    • Given: L1 is on the list once
    • When: the same Tool Checked Out for L1 is applied again
    • Then: L1 is still on the list once.
  • Replayed sent notice (INV-OLN-3, INV-OLN-9)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for L1, so L1 is off the list
    • When: the same Overdue Notice Sent is applied again
    • Then: L1 is still off the list.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-OLN-9). An event applied a second time leaves the list as it was after the first.
  • Events for a loan that has left the list: once a loan's row is removed, a later Loan Extended, Tool Returned or Tool Lost for it (a replay) changes nothing. An Overdue Notice Failed doesn't reach this list at all.
  • The gateway reads a loan twice before Overdue Notice Sent lands: the list may return the same loan on two reads in a row. Sending one notice per loan is the Send Overdue Notice slice's rule, enforced when it records Overdue Notice Sent; this list raises no errors of its own.
  • Daylight-saving changes: the day boundary is midnight in the shed's local time zone, whatever its offset from UTC that day.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: read only by the Overdue Notice Gateway. No person or screen reads it.
  • PII & compliance: holds the name and current email of every registered neighbor, and hands them to the gateway only for borrowers with an overdue loan. It shows them on no screen.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above. A loan is ready as soon as it joins the list; how soon the email goes out after that is Send Overdue Notice's concern.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId, name, email.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Overdue Notice Sent (Send Overdue Notice): loanId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • These match slices/add-tool.md, slices/register-neighbor.md, slices/check-out-tool.md, slices/extend-loan.md and slices/my-loans.md. Change Email, Send Overdue Notice, Return Tool and Record Tool Lost are specified in slices not yet written in depth; these keys are this view's assumptions, and each is checked when that slice is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Send Overdue Notice, whose gateway works from this list and records Overdue Notice Sent.

Open Questions

None.
